goods.name: Pearls
goods.blurb: Beautiful deep-water pearls. Perfect for jewellery or a wedding gift.
goods.nature: Otters grow pearls in the shallow beds off Tassel's rafts and pick them by hand. A wedding needs three, so most of them never leave the water they grew in. Emberkin houses buy them thirty at a time.

goods.name: Tide glass
goods.blurb: Beautiful sea glass. Perfect for decoration or pressure vessels.
goods.nature: Otters forge tideglass in the volcanic trenches beneath Tassel's ocean. It is perfect for the underwater cities down in the cold depths. Other species simply find it beautiful.

goods.name: Moonfish oil
goods.blurb: Clean-burning fish oil. Perfect for lamps, cooking or waterproofing.
goods.nature: Otters press it out of a fish that only surfaces on the dark of the moon, on Tassel's open water. It burns clean and keeps forever, which is most of why anybody carries it. It also smells so exactly of a harbour that homesick otters buy a jar simply to open it.

goods.name: Coral carvings
goods.blurb: Carved reef coral. Perfect for a gift, and otters give a great many gifts.
goods.nature: Otters cut it from the living reefs under Tassel and finish each piece with a thumb, which takes about a year of evenings. They are made to be given rather than sold. One that turns up in a market has usually come out of a household that broke up, and the buyers know it.

goods.name: Shiny moon pebbles
goods.blurb: Smooth grey moon rocks. No otter can walk past one.
goods.nature: Otters have been picking up shiny rocks since long before they had ships, and leaving the water has not cured it. These are offcuts, tumbled smooth in the Slate yards and swept off the floor by the crate. Every otter who buys one knows that, and buys one anyway.

goods.name: Iron ore
goods.blurb: Heavy crates of nickel-iron. Perfect for anybody with a furnace.
goods.nature: Dug out of Slate and Scorch, sorted, and nothing else done to it at all. On its own it is worth almost nothing. Put it near a furnace and it becomes whatever the smith felt like making that week.

goods.name: Engraved masonry
goods.blurb: Heavy patterned stone. Perfect for terraces and anything built to last.
goods.nature: Quarried and carved on Slate, where the yards cut stone to the same tolerances they cut hulls. The old patterns go on every block, including the faces that will be buried. Nothing lighter will hold up a terrace, and a terrace is meant to outlast the argument that built it.

goods.name: Medicinal herbs
goods.blurb: Field-cut medicinal herbs. Perfect for a dispensary or a long voyage.
goods.nature: Cut green and bundled by hand on Moss, off terraces somebody's great-grandmother laid out. Half the remedies anyone takes anywhere start as this. A physician can tell a wet-cut bundle from a good one by the squeak, and will tell you so at length.

goods.name: Starfruit wine
goods.blurb: Pale starfruit wine. Perfect for a celebration, or for showing off.
goods.nature: Grown and pressed on Moss in runs too small to go round, which is deliberate. It is pale, faintly sharp, and does not travel especially well. Scarcity is most of the flavour and the growers have understood that for six generations.

goods.name: Glowmoss
goods.blurb: Living lamp-moss in a jar. Perfect for tunnels, holds and dark corners.
goods.nature: Grown on Moss in sheds nobody is allowed to open in daylight. It wants no fuel, no air and no attention, and it never goes out. Anyone who lives underground ends up with green corridors and stops noticing.

goods.name: Rare riverfish
goods.blurb: Rare silver riverfish. Needs a cold hold. Cats pay a great deal.
goods.nature: Out of three rivers on Moss and nowhere else, and quick enough that catching one is a story before it is a meal. Fresh, it is magnificent. Warm, it is an apology, which is why nobody ships it without a cold hold.

goods.name: Spare engine parts
goods.blurb: Heavy crates of engine spares. Perfect for a refit, or an emergency.
goods.nature: Valves, seals and struts, packed in oiled paper by the Cinder forges that made them. Nobody has ever bought a crate of these excited. Far from a dry dock they are the difference between a ship and a wreck, and out there nobody asks the price twice.

goods.name: Weapons
goods.blurb: Heavy crated house arms. Emberkin houses buy them constantly.
goods.nature: Made on Cinder, crated, and sealed with the mark of whoever ordered them. The Emberkin are proud, competitive and extremely well armed. There are feuds running eleven years that have never fired a shot and have never once stopped buying.

goods.name: Heat-resistant plating
goods.blurb: Heavy heat-resistant sheet. Perfect for hulls that go somewhere hot.
goods.nature: Rolled on Cinder, which has more experience of heat than anywhere else and mentions it often. It will sit in a cloud top all day and come out grumbling. Half the shielded hulls in the sky are wearing it, including, if you have one, yours.

goods.name: Refined steel
goods.blurb: Heavy graded bar stock. Perfect for absolutely anything.
goods.nature: Melted, rolled and stamped on Cinder, and the least interesting thing they make there. Every yard in the system is short of it, because nobody plans for steel and everybody uses steel. It is the dullest cargo you can carry and it always sells.

goods.name: Reactor coils
goods.blurb: Hand-wound reactor coils. Perfect for a refit or a failing reactor.
goods.nature: Emberkin smiths on Cinder wind each coil by hand over nine days, in an order they have never written down. Nothing else will make a reactor behave. Cats will trade a whole ship for a crate of them.

goods.name: Fire crystals
goods.blurb: Bright fire crystals. Needs a cold hold. Perfect for lighting a grand room.
goods.nature: Grown in the vents on Scorch and cut cold by miners paid by the stone. Kept cold, one holds a light for a week after the sun comes off it. Let one warm and it gives the whole week back at once, which is spectacular and expensive.

goods.name: Volcanic glass
goods.blurb: Heavy sheets of black glass. Perfect for blades, windows or floors.
goods.nature: Cut off the lava flows on Scorch and packed in ash for the journey. It is cheap there because there is nothing else there. It is cheap everywhere else because everybody has already worked out that it cuts.

goods.name: Emberstone
goods.blurb: Warm emberstone. Perfect for a hearth, or for sleeping beside.
goods.nature: Dug out of Scorch, and still warm to the hand a year later. Nobody has ever explained why, and the official Scorch position is that it came out of the ground warm and will go back in warm. Cats buy them to sleep on, which is the most sensible use anyone has found.

goods.name: Ember silk
goods.blurb: This season's ember silk. Sells for double until the colour turns.
goods.nature: Woven on Veyra in a heated room, because it leaves the loom the colour of ash and will not take dye below ninety degrees. The season's colour changes four times a year. The dyers know the next one before anybody else does, and dress accordingly.

goods.name: Faction medals
goods.blurb: Struck faction medals. Perfect for settling a score in public.
goods.nature: Struck on Veyra in small numbers, for houses with something to prove and an audience to prove it to. The metal is worth very little. The name struck into it ends an argument in the only way some houses accept that an argument can be ended.

goods.name: Precision clocks
goods.blurb: Precision clocks. Otters buy them by the raft and then argue.
goods.nature: Built on Veyra to a second a month, which is the difference between planning a launch window and guessing at one. Only two sorts of person need that: a ship's navigator, and an Emberkin, whose year runs fifty-six days. No otter household will admit to owning one alone, so a raft buys one together and argues all season about whose shelf it sits on.

goods.name: Perfume oils
goods.blurb: Small bottles of perfume oil. Perfect for a gift, or an impression.
goods.nature: Distilled on Veyra a drop at a time, from flowers grown for nothing else. What costs money is not the scent but the sameness: it took four years to make the blend repeat. Half the system finds them ridiculous and buys them anyway.

goods.name: Storm crystals
goods.blurb: Storm crystals, still ticking. Cats pay a great deal and go quiet.
goods.nature: Fished off Grumm's cloud tops on a line, out of weather that was running long before anyone arrived to watch it. They are still ticking when they reach you and nobody is certain what they are. Cats hold one up to a lamp and stop talking, which cats otherwise never do.

goods.name: Advanced filters
goods.blurb: Heavy frog-made air filters. Perfect anywhere people breathe indoors.
goods.nature: Built in the floating cities of Grumm, by people who have had a long time to think about air. They are better than anything the inner worlds can manage. The makers will explain exactly how, at length, twice, and you will still not be able to do it.

goods.name: Ancient cider
goods.blurb: Ten-thousand-year-old cider. Needs a cold hold. Otters pay most.
goods.nature: Laid down in a balloon city over Grumm some fifty frog generations ago, for drinkers who had not hatched. The cellar has been moved four times and never once opened in a hurry. Otters weep at it, and the frogs consider weeping the correct response.

goods.name: Medicinal gel
goods.blurb: Medicinal gel. Needs a cold hold. Closes wounds nothing else will.
goods.nature: Brewed on the apothecary rafts at Brine, where the chemistry does things it will not do on a warm world. Cold, it will close a wound nothing else will touch. Warm it once and it is soup, which has happened to enough pilots that there is a word for them.

goods.name: Brine amber
goods.blurb: Brine amber with something inside it. Perfect for a collection.
goods.nature: Fished out of the ammonia sea at Brine with something set inside that is not a leaf: six arms, folded, and a seam down the middle that has been open and shut. Nothing in that sea has bones. Collectors pay for the pieces where you can see the seam.

goods.name: Sea-foam resin
goods.blurb: Sea-foam resin. Perfect for repairs of very nearly any kind.
goods.nature: Skimmed off the foam at Brine and sold in tubs. It sets hard in vacuum and stays very slightly soft forever, so it holds where nothing rigid would. A crate of it will fix almost anything, and whoever does the fixing will do it in front of you, slowly, explaining.

goods.name: Ice lenses
goods.blurb: Ground ice lenses. Needs a cold hold. Perfect for charts or long looks.
goods.nature: Ground at Glass from shell ice that has never once melted, and will not survive meeting anything that has. You can read a ship's name off one from further than you would believe. The scholars who grind them are mildly embarrassed about what most buyers use them for.

goods.name: Cryo fuel
goods.blurb: Heavy bulk cryogenic fuel. Perfect for refrigeration or smelting.
goods.nature: Frogs draw it from under the ice shell at Glass and ship it out in double-walled crates. Everything cold in the system runs on it. They think it is the dullest thing they make and are frankly glad somebody wants it.

goods.name: Moon incense
goods.blurb: Slow-burning moon incense. Perfect for a festival or a long think.
goods.nature: Rolled in silence on Croak, by people who chose to live somewhere expensive to reach. It burns slowly and travels badly. Most of what it costs is the getting there, which the ascetics find funny and will not lower the price over.

goods.name: Pilgrim beads
goods.blurb: Strung pilgrim beads. Cheap, and worth more once they have travelled.
goods.nature: Strung one bead a day for a year on Croak, which is the whole of the making. A pilgrim carries a string out and carries it back again. The ones that have been somewhere cost more than the ones that have not, which is the only honest price anybody puts on distance.

goods.name: Ancient frog tea
goods.blurb: Ancient pressed tea. Otters pay most, and pay a great deal.
goods.nature: Pressed into bricks on Croak longer ago than the records go, and the frogs keep excellent records. A brick is broken for a guest and not otherwise. Having one broken for you when you are only passing through is a considerable thing, and you will not be allowed to refuse.

goods.name: Prayer lanterns
goods.blurb: Paper prayer lanterns. Perfect for the turn of the year.
goods.nature: Folded on Haven from paper and wire, with a wish written inside where nobody reads it. They all go up at once at the year's turn. For about an hour the sky over the terraces is unusable, and every pilot within range knows to wait.

goods.name: Festival dyes
goods.blurb: Bright festival dyes. Perfect for cloth, banners or a very good party.
goods.nature: Ground on Haven into twists of waxed cloth, for a festival that has never once been cancelled. They cost almost nothing where they are made, because everyone has some. Somewhere else, somebody has worked out what else they will colour, and pays accordingly.

goods.name: Frogwood instruments
goods.blurb: Heavy frogwood instruments. Perfect for a hall, or a very good raft.
goods.nature: Built on Haven from wood that grows on one terrace, and tuned over a lifetime — the maker's, and then whoever gets it next. They are heavy, slow to make, and worth what is asked for them. An otter who hears one played properly stops talking, which otters otherwise do not do.

goods.name: Salvaged ship plating
goods.blurb: Heavy salvaged hull plate. Perfect for a repair on a budget.
goods.nature: Cut off whatever came into Nail last, straightened, and stacked by thickness. Every sheet of it was somebody's ship. The cats who sell it do not mention whose, which they say is manners rather than superstition.

goods.name: Rebuilt thrusters
goods.blurb: Heavy rebuilt thrusters. Perfect for a refit at half the price.
goods.nature: Stripped, cleaned and rebuilt at Nail by somebody who mainly wanted to settle an argument about how they ought to have been built. They generally come back better than they left the factory. The cat who did it will want to know how it flew, and will remember your answer for years.

goods.name: Salvaged sensors
goods.blurb: Salvaged sensor arrays. Working, mostly. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: Pulled out of wrecks and off the ring by the salvagers at Nail, and tested about as carefully as you would expect. Most of them work. The ones cut out of the ring see a great deal further than they are supposed to, and those do not go to just anybody.

goods.name: Arc fragments
goods.blurb: A fragment of Builder metal. The dearest cargo there is. Frogs pay well.
goods.nature: Cut off the ring and brought in through Nail, where the cats have been quietly taking it apart for generations. It has no join, no tooling mark, and no way to tell which way up it is meant to go. Tap it and it hums — and so does every other piece ever cut off the ring, at exactly the same note.

goods.name: Stolen Ember weapons
goods.blurb: Heavy crates of Emberkin arms, marks filed off. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: House arms that came through Whisker without paperwork, with the crest filed off by somebody in a hurry; a thumb still finds it. Nobody at Whisker asks where they came from and nobody expects to be told. Most of them go home again at a markup, bought back by the houses that lost them.

goods.name: Counterfeit faction medals
goods.blurb: Counterfeit faction medals. Cheap, and extremely convincing.
goods.nature: Struck at Whisker this morning and aged this afternoon by a cat who takes real pride in the work. They are good enough that the houses named on them buy them. Whether that is funny or a little sad depends entirely on which house you ask.

goods.name: Smuggled medicine
goods.blurb: Unlabelled medicine. Needs a cold hold. Worth most where the real thing is priced out.
goods.nature: The same crates as the legitimate ones, routed through Whisker and sold at half of what they should cost. The apothecaries who brewed it know exactly where it ends up and have never once complained. Everybody involved regards this as a public service conducted slightly sideways.

goods.name: Cybernetic body parts
goods.blurb: Replacement hands, eyes and spines. Cats pay most.
goods.nature: Made to order and sold through Whisker, because the inner worlds have strong opinions about who should be allowed to sell them. A cat who has lost something to vacuum would rather not discuss it with a licensing board. They cost a fortune, and nobody who needs one haggles.

cinder.notes: Engine smiths; the cheapest fuel in the system straight from the refineries.

scorch.notes: Mining frontier. Cheap rock, dangerous work, and the Emberkin nobody at home writes to.

veyra.notes: Auction houses and money. Everything is for sale and everybody is watching who buys it.

tassel.notes: The gossip hub and starting port. Big market, honest prices, terrible secrets.

slate.notes: Dry docks and cranes. Tanks and holds are fitted here, as they are anywhere with a pump, and here they come with commentary.

moss.notes: Farming moon, green to the shoreline. Will sell you grain and fruit and ask where you bank.

nail.notes: Belt haven. Repairs, salvage and a bar. Match speeds and knock.

whisker.notes: The shady end of the Belt. No questions, no paperwork, and a fitter who works in the dark.

arc.notes: Cat salvagers camped on the rim of a Builder ring, riding just beyond the Belt. No fuel; bring your own or beg.

grumm.notes: Balloon cities in the cold upper clouds. The trade window for the whole frog system.

brine.notes: Ammonia seas and floating apothecaries. Chemistry nobody else can read.

glass.notes: Research station over an ocean under ice. They study the Builders and will talk your ear off.

croak.notes: Retrograde and austere. Barely a market. The approach is dear on purpose.

haven.notes: The frog capital and the outer system’s great market. No haggling; prices are exchange rates and goodwill.

maw.notes: No market. Something down there is still keeping station.

upgrades.name: Stock tank
upgrades.effect: The tank the ship came with (size from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Tassel's moons, the Belt, and a loose capture at Grumm.

upgrades.name: Long-haul tank
upgrades.unlocks: Cinder and the inward run, where the arrival is most of the bill.

upgrades.name: Deep-sky tank
upgrades.effect: Larger Δv budget again (size from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: Grumm and Haven without counting every metre; the Arc with room to come home.

upgrades.name: Deep-dark tank
upgrades.unlocks: The Maw, and running hot anywhere you like.

upgrades.name: Stock hold
upgrades.effect: The hold the ship came with (units from tuning; the sim assumes 24).
upgrades.unlocks: One consignment at a time, and not a large one.

upgrades.name: Raft hold
upgrades.unlocks: Bulk runs that actually pay: ore and steel by the crate rather than the armful.

upgrades.name: Barge hold
upgrades.effect: Larger cargo capacity again (units from tuning).
upgrades.unlocks: A delivery and a speculation in the same hold.

upgrades.name: Barn hold
upgrades.unlocks: Ore and masonry by the barge, and a full frog gift-exchange in one trip.

upgrades.name: Gravitational sensors
upgrades.effect: See gravitational phenomena on the chart.
upgrades.unlocks: Finds what bends a course and does not shine. There are two such things: one between Tassel and the Belt, and one at the far edge, which is what the Dancer has been going round all this time.

upgrades.name: Temperature control
upgrades.effect: The hold can carry goods that will not keep at hold temperature.
upgrades.unlocks: Rare riverfish, fire crystals, ancient cider, ice lenses, medicinal gel and smuggled medicine.

upgrades.name: The Astrolabe
upgrades.effect: Reads the transfer window to every world that goes round the Lamp: what a crossing would cost today, and how many days until it is cheap.
upgrades.unlocks: Interplanetary work. No harbourmaster will hand you a job that leaves their own sky without one.

upgrades.name: Heat shielding
upgrades.effect: Survive a skim through a world’s air, and let it slow you down.
upgrades.unlocks: Air braking at Veyra, Cinder, Tassel, Grumm and Brine — everywhere there is air to brake in. The deeper the pass, the more it shakes the hull.

upgrades.name: Cryo hull cooling
upgrades.effect: Carries the heat of a skim away as fast as the air makes it.
upgrades.unlocks: Air braking with no risk to the hull at all, however deep you go.

price.description: You pay base * sells.priceMul * mood * (1 - repDiscount). A port pays base * demand * (needsTempControl ? tempControlMul : 1) * mood * (1 + repDiscount/2). Nothing else moves a price: what you have sold here before does not, and how picked-over a shelf is does not. The stall's stock is the only limit on how much of a thing you can move at once, and that is limit enough.

reputation.description: Reputation is 0..10 points per species. Purchases and fuel at that species' ports are discounted by min(maxDiscount, discountPerPoint*points). Frog gifts scale with frog reputation; cat tolls fall by the same fraction.

toll.description: A Belt toll intercept takes min(cap, fraction*cargoValue) in goods, chosen by the cats; nothing if cargoValue < minCargoValue (they never take everything and never harm a ship that yields). There is nothing to hide behind: the only let-off is the cooldown, so a captain is never asked twice inside a month.

tow.description: A stranded or crashed ship is towed to the nearest port: cost = base + perAu*distanceAu, time = max(3, daysPerAu*distanceAu) days. If you cannot pay, the Tassel harbour bank fronts it and the debt is deducted from sales.

haggle.description: Otter ports: each visit rolls a uniform spread of +-spread on every price, then a haggle mini-exchange lets you keep the good end of the roll. Frogs never haggle (spread 0). Cats and Emberkin do not haggle either.

volatility.description: Daily random-walk wobble on what a port pays, amplitude by species. Emberkin markets are the most volatile. This is species character, not supply and demand: it does not remember anything you did.

speciesRules.otter: Haggle spread: every price at an otter port is rolled within +-spread, per good, per day. The roll is the whole of it — there is no haggling exchange behind it.
speciesRules.emberkin: Volatile prices: what Cinder wants this week is not what it wanted last week.
speciesRules.cat: Tolls in the Belt under strict custom (never everything, never a ship that yields). Impress a captain and a gift may follow.
speciesRules.frog: No haggling. "Prices" are exchange rates: you are paid in trade credit at the stall plus goodwill (reputation), and every visit ends with a gift.

stock.description: A stall's shelves hold a number rolled out of the good's own stock range, and they are rolled again when you come back from somewhere else. Staying at one dock and waiting does not restock it; going and trading elsewhere does. What you bought this visit is what is missing, and the price does not move as the shelf empties: the shelf itself is the limit.

demand.description: What a port pays for a good, as a multiple of its base price. Two questions: does this port want it (loved, on its buyer list, or neither), and is it out of the good's own region. Space is hard and there are few interspecies merchants, so carrying a loved good to another people is the trade the game is about; the same run inside one system is worth a fraction of it. Regions are named in the ports table: inner, home, belt, outer, deep.

sim.notes: Reference figures the balance work was done against, kept here so a tuning change can be checked against what it was meant to be. Not read by the game: the build strips this block out.

regions.inner: The Emberkin worlds: Cinder, Scorch and Veyra.
regions.home: Tassel and its moons, Slate and Moss.
regions.belt: The Belt: Nail, Whisker and the Arc.
regions.outer: Grumm and its moons: Brine, Glass, Croak and Haven.
